outcome: hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn
cohort: 150 pregnant women attending an antenatal clinic at a federal teaching hospital in Nigeria
finding: 4.7% of the pregnant women had positive alloantibody screens, of which 1.33% were clinically significant maternal alloantibodies (Anti-D and Anti-Lub), and no statistically significant association was observed between alloimmunization and variables such as gestational age, parity, hemoglobin phenotype, previous blood transfusions, and Rh D negativity.
gest_age: Participants were in various stages of pregnancy: 9.3% in the first trimester, 60% in the third trimester (the stage for the rest was not specified).
